newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-OPINION-Louthean on Australian Mining - Gawler Craton beckons.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-OPINION-Louthean on Australian Mining - Gawler Craton beckons.

text.p: Steve Elliott got to work with the long spade to prove a point.

The lanky geologist and Helix Resources Ltd director wanted to show the presence of calcrete in a sandy soil-covered area in the Lake Everard district of South Australia -- an area seemingly populated only by geologists, field hands, snakes, wombats and sheep.

The lumps of calcrete he picked up at less than 0.2 of a metre was the signature Helix wants in the quest for gold and perhaps polymetallic targets on the Lake Everard block, about 50 km south of Tarcoola.
Helix is in the heartland of the Gawler Craton, a massive geological structure that takes in Eyre Peninsula and a vast area to the west and north.
